To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated the Förster resonance energy harvesting in the arrays of epitaxially grown CdSe quantum dots (QD) embedded into a ZnSe matrix, which provides the efficient excitation of large QDs by small QDs.
Förster resonance energy harvesting is observed in arrays of epitaxially grown CdSe/ZnSe fractional monolayer quantum dots (QD), where QDs of different size are in close proximity.

Förster energy transfer between the ground levels and excited states of QDs can be used for the excitation of the radiative QDs and that this mechanism is efficient for a wide range of distances between the donor and acceptor QDs.

the Förster resonance energy (FRET) and harvesting in II-VI quantum dot (QD) monolayer arrays.
the energy transfer in II–VI quantum dot arrays, formed by fractional monodispersed CdSe monolayer insertions in ZnSe matrices.
Förster resonance energy (FRET) in the dense arrays formed by epitaxial quantum dot (QD) insertions within a semiconductor matrix.

we have demonstrated the energy transfer between different sized QDs in a monolayer array of CdSe QDs in ZnSe matrix.
we have shown the possibility of controlling the energy transfer in QD arrays by varying the size of QDs and the density of the QD arrays.
Förster resonance energy (FRET) transfer is an effective mechanism of energy harvesting and directional emission of photons in the QD-based nanostructures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Förster energy transfer in the QD array can be used to harvest the excitons in the ground states of small QDs, and to transfer them to the radiating large QDs.

we have shown the possibility to control energy transfer between the QDs of various sizes in the dense arrays, which is important for the design of the nanostructures for the light harvesting applications.
Förster resonance energy transfers can be used for the harvesting of exciton energy from the dense arrays of the QDs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exciton-exciton interaction in QD arrays can be used for engineering the energy level structure in QD arrays, and for designing efficient nano-emitters.
